reasons.A: Long, impersonal instructional sentences with subordinate clauses, a semicolon and a colon; none of the passage's clipped first-person rhythm or dry asides.
reasons.B: Right register (short declaratives, no contractions, first person), but it stacks fragments far more densely than the passage ('Not all of them. The wool ones.', 'Not stretched. Just flat.'), reading as imitation.
reasons.C: Mostly complete short sentences with the occasional fragment and longer sentence, plain first person, no contractions, and a dry aside ('it was in the drawer anyway') close to the passage's 'I do not regret it'; nearest in movement and stance.
